title: Maple-Roasted Carrots & Parsnips
subtitle: Ontario winter roots roasted hot, then tossed in maple butter until the edges caramelize
imageAlt: Maple-roasted carrot and parsnip batons with caramelized edges on a white oval platter
servingsNote: Christmas side for two, plus leftovers

beforeYouStart.text: A hot oven, 220°C (425°F), and plenty of room on the sheet are what make them caramelize.
Cut everything to the same size so it all finishes together.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Cut the carrots and parsnips into batons about 8 cm long and 1.5 cm thick. Halve or quarter the thick parsnip tops to match, and cut out the core if it's woody.

steps.title: Season and roast
steps.text: Toss on the sheet with the oil, salt, pepper and dried thyme, then spread in one layer with space between. Roast 20 minutes.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Stir the maple syrup and melted butter together, drizzle over the vegetables and toss. Roast 10–12 minutes more, until tender with caramelized edges.

fixIt.fix: The pan was crowded. Use two sheets, or move it to the top rack for the last 5 minutes.
Add the maple only for the last 10–12 minutes. Sugar burns at this heat.
Large parsnips have a woody core. Cut it out next time.

saleTip: Ontario carrots and parsnips are cheapest in 2 lb bags all winter, about $2.50–3.50 a bag at No Frills.
swap: All carrots works fine, or use sweet potato for the parsnips (same size, same time). Honey works instead of maple.
leftovers: Warm in a pan for a side, or blend with hot broth into a quick soup.
doneness: Done when a knife slides into the thickest parsnip piece with no resistance and the edges are browned.
source: Based on tested maple-roasted root vegetable methods (Canadian Living, Ricardo): roasted at 220°C (425°F), glazed with maple for the last 10 minutes.
prepAhead: Peel and cut the vegetables up to 2 days ahead; keep in a sealed container in the fridge with a damp paper towel.
reheat: Spread on a sheet at 200°C (400°F) for 8–10 minutes until hot, or microwave 1–2 minutes.

basic.note: Maple alone: no butter or dried thyme.

stepNotes.2: Basic: oil, salt and pepper only.
stepNotes.3: Basic: drizzle the maple syrup on its own.
Fancy: scatter the pecans over the vegetables for the last 5 minutes so they toast.

plating: Pile the batons criss-cross on a warm platter.
Spoon any maple butter from the sheet over the top.
Pecans last, so they stay crunchy.

why.0-1: Parsnips are sweet and nutty once roasted; they brown faster than carrots, so cut them a touch thicker.
why.1-0: Maple added late caramelizes without burning.

funFact: Parsnips taste sweeter after a frost: the cold turns some of their starch into sugar, which is why they're a winter vegetable in Ontario.

keeps.note: roasted carrots and parsnips turn soft and watery once thawed
